chunk_map.heading: H1/lede — Fork the worktree, carry the evidence
Anchor the fork to the run coordinates

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a slide-viewer stranded on a pronoun/demonstrative with no in-file antecedent. Checked every chunk: chunk 0's 'the session you sent off from' is the session-artifacts carve-out (student's own live session); chunk 1's prompt is self-contained; chunk 2's 'the output'/'the worktree path' continue chunk 1's own prompt-and-response; chunk 3's 'Run coordinates' block and 'M4 starting point' commit were both first named inside chunk 1's prompt text and are reused, not invented. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found — harm absent.

Harm: a slide pointing at another file by position ('the opening lecture said'). No body text names another file at all (the only cross-file reference, 'learn-from-the-test.md', sits in the maintainer block below the cut) — harm not applicable to this body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the current module set doesn't have. The only backward-looking mentions are the session-artifact carve-out ('the session you sent off from') and 'the M4 rules and observations' — both point at real, current prior-module state (M4), not a removed beat. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal beat broken by the reveal landing above the guess. No guess/predict construct anywhere in this file's body — harm not applicable.

Harm: a chunk that projects as content-free (a lone wait-state bullet). Every chunk carries multiple substantive, self-carrying bullets or a full prompt block — none is a bare context-dependent fragment. Harm absent.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. This is the previously-flagged chunk: heading is now 'Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (pre-extraction title), and content is the normal-case read of Run coordinates plus two fallback bullets — the header covers both, it no longer promises fallback-only content while opening with the success path. Harm resolved; re-derived independently, not taken on the maintainer note's word.

Harm: visible LLM tics (Not-X-Not-Y-Z, anaphora triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction-noun stacks, empty-leg verb triplets) turning a slide into filler. Scanned every chunk for each sub-item: none present. Harm absent across all sub-items.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) landing on a projected slide where an engineer in the room has no context for it. Body uses only ordinary or arc-earned terms (session, worktree, branch, commit, task.md) — no maintainer dialect in chunks 0-3. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold used on whole narrative lead sentences instead of short handles, exceeding the ≤1-bolded-element norm. Chunk 0's bolds ('Time:', 'Session', 'What you do:', 'What you build:', 'The point:') are the standard exercise-widget label pattern, each ≲3 words, not narrative leads; chunks 1-3 carry no body bold outside the fenced prompt (exempt). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: rules 1-9 evaluated against a section absent from the composed Slides deck (phase-less prose dropped by buildDeckModel). This file's sections sit inside the standard exercise wrapper structure used throughout AE101 exercises — no reason to suspect deck-absence, and this rule is a presence gate, not a per-chunk content rule to score PASS/REVISE on. Harm not applicable here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered slide position, or a 'Phase K'/'Step K' reference that doesn't resolve in-file. Only one phase header exists ('Phase 1: Fork it'), no other phase is referenced elsewhere in this file, so there is no sequence or cross-reference to break. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a body pointer aimed at page position ('below', 'above', 'at the top of this page') that resolves to nothing once the renderer cuts at ##. No such geometry language appears anywhere in the body. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an in-body link that doesn't earn its place, or is located by page geometry rather than named. The body carries zero in-body links (the one cross-doc pointer, '[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]', sits in the maintainer block below the cut, exempt). Harm not applicable.
